title: Unlocking the Potential of Weighting Methods in Federated Learning Through Communication Compression
claim: Our compressed method nearly matches its uncompressed version and beats compressed baselines, especially under heterogeneous data and aggressive compression.
layout: 2x2 grid of line plots, rows by compressor, columns by data heterogeneity
description: Four accuracy-versus-communication-rounds line plots in a 2x2 grid on light blue backgrounds with dashed grid lines. The top row, captioned (a) Rand50% compressor, and the bottom row, captioned (b) Rand10% compressor, each have an i.i.d. panel on the left and a non-i.i.d. panel on the right. Each panel shows four curves with markers: ADI (no comp.) in red with circles, ADI in green with squares, DIANA in orange with stars, and EF21 in dark blue with triangles. Accuracy rises from about 10 to the 80s-90 over 10000 rounds. ADI curves sit on top, close to the uncompressed one. DIANA is slightly below them. EF21 is lowest and noisiest, especially in the non-i.i.d. and Rand10% panels. The legend is in the lower right of each panel.
caption: Performance comparison for ADI across different heterogeneity levels.
abstract: Modern machine learning problems are frequently formulated in federated learning domain and incorporate inherently heterogeneous data. Weighting methods operate efficiently in terms of iteration complexity and represent a common direction in this setting. At the same time, they do not address directly the main obstacle in federated and distributed learning -- communication bottleneck. We tackle this issue by incorporating compression into the weighting scheme. We establish the convergence under a convexity assumption, considering both exact and stochastic oracles. Finally, we evaluate the practical performance of the proposed method on real-world problems.
